author: Rob Loach
install_msg: Retro installed. Load it with `[p]load retro`, then attach a ROM to `[p]retro` and play, or run `[p]retro list` to see what this bot can start. The console emulators download themselves in the background on the first load, so give them a minute. Upgrading? See the README.
name: Retro
short: Play retro console games in Discord
description:
Play retro console games together in Discord, emulated with libretro.

Start a game by name, URL, or an attached ROM or .zip and control it with buttons under the screen. Every press posts an animated clip of the next second of play. Nine consoles, from the NES to the Game Boy Advance, each with its own controller layout, picked from the file extension.

Games save automatically and resume where they left off, even after the bot restarts. Undo steps back through the last eight presses.
end_user_data_statement: This cog stores the Discord channel and message ID of each game, the ID of the member who started it, the name of the game being played, and a copy of the ROM together with its emulator save state and the game's own in-game save, so a game can be resumed later. The same details are kept for the few most recent games a channel has moved on from, so their Resume buttons keep working. Those records are deleted by the cog itself once they can no longer resume anything: when the channel or thread is deleted, when the bot leaves the server, or when the cached ROM they name is cleaned up. Deleting a record removes the member ID in it; the game's save state and in-game save are kept, because they belong to the channel rather than to any member. The clip on a game's message is an attachment on that message and is not stored anywhere else; the server display name of whoever last pressed a button appears in that message's text, as plain text that cannot notify anyone, and is not stored anywhere either; the save states the Undo button steps back through are stored beside that game's save state and are deleted with it. Members with the Manage Messages permission, whoever started a game, and the bot owner can export a copy of a game's saves into the channel, replace them with an uploaded file, or delete them. Nothing is shared with anyone automatically. Cached ROMs, save states and in-game saves are pruned automatically as a channel plays other games.
